neuter noun

in grammar

also neuter gender, neuter noun, in the neuter

classical

Quint. 1.4.24: neutrālī fēminās significant
Quint. 1.5.54 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 247

neutrālis, neutrāle

of the neuter gender

Quintilian’s word: nōmina neutrālia. Adverb neutrāliter, in the neuter (Traupman 247).

Other words

  • neuter, neutra, neutrum — neuter; of verbs, neither active nor passive

    also used · classical · Cic. Or. 155; Gell. 1.7.15 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 221, 247

    The grammarians’ phrase is neutrī generis, of the neuter gender (Charisius, Diomedes), and Traupman’s genus neutrum (221). Verba neutra are verbs neither active nor passive, that is intransitive (see intransitive).

Examples

  • neutrāliter

    in the neuterTraupman 350

See also gender, masculine, feminine, intransitive.
